The Start Page

The first tab is the front door. Under the mark and the version it says what is new in this release and offers the two-minute tour. Continue is the project you are on (the level with its picture and best score, or the sandbox with its parts and rungs), Open a file… and New project. The levels are a plant floor: one station per graded level, easiest first, lit as you get them running, and a tile per level with its picture, difficulty and best score; a station or a tile opens its level straight away. Down the left is the help, a section per feature, with a search box over the help and your project.

A new project

File → New Project… is a catalogue. A rail down the left jumps to its sections and lights up as you scroll; every option is a picture card of it running, with a title, one line and a chip that says what kind of project it is, and More… unfolds the full description.

  • Graded levels — the 22 levels as tiles, in order of difficulty, each with your best score and whether it is in progress (Part V).
  • Start — an Empty project: a bare floor and an empty routine, where Part IV begins.
  • Guided — Build the bottle line (the same empty floor, with the lesson panel), Servo axis and Sample sorter.
  • Classic scenes — the elevator, the traffic intersection, the parking entry gate, the roll-up warehouse door, the car wash and a busy car wash, the air compressor room, the material silo and the inspection line (Part VI).
  • Sandboxes — the sample sorter scene, the servo axis, the LogixPro-style Bottle Line and the Card Sort Cell.

The LogixPro-style Bottle Line is the finished machine of Part IV with its program already written, in fifteen step routines, mix kitchen included. It is your answer key: build from the empty floor, and when a lesson will not behave, open the finished line and compare. The Guided menu has the guided projects too, and a fourth, the Code Reader.

Nothing is thrown away when you switch. Each level keeps its own floor and program, so opening Level 3 and then Level 6 and back finds Level 3 as you left it; the sandbox project you were on when you opened a level is kept as Your sandbox project on the Start Page.

Save, open, share, export

Save Ctrl+S writes the whole project — scene, tags, routines, panel layout, trends — as one JSON file; Open… Ctrl+O reads it back. Share Link… packs the project into a link — compressed and written into the address itself, so nothing is uploaded anywhere — and Open Link… unpacks one. Export / Copy as Text… gives the program as rung text you can paste anywhere, which is also how this book’s listings were made. Export L5X writes a Studio 5000 import file with your tags and routines; Import L5X reads one, including Add-On Instructions. New Controller clears tags and rungs but keeps the scene — the fastest way to start Part IV’s programming lessons on a machine you have already built.

The page also keeps your work between visits by itself, in the browser’s storage; Save is for a copy you can carry, send or keep.

Watch for

The two Load Reference Solution entries replace your program. Complete Bottle Line (15 steps) installs Part IV’s fifteen routines on the LogixPro-style scene and adds any part the floor is missing; the plain one installs the older single-routine answer. Save first if you have rungs you want to keep.

Download and upload

As in Logix Designer, there are two copies of the program: the project you edit here and the program in the controller. Edits made offline change only the project; the controller keeps running what it was given until you download. Going online (Communications → Go Online, the Run button, or the key switch menu) compares the two. If they match, you go straight online. If they differ, Connect To Go Online says how — the controller is empty, it holds another project, or which routines and how many tags changed offline — and offers three choices.

ChoiceWhat happens
DownloadThe project goes to the controller. The controller goes to Remote Program first, so the logic stops scanning and the outputs drop. The controller’s tag values are replaced with the project’s: counters, timers, FIFOs and anything the HMI wrote start over. If you asked for Run, it then offers to change the controller back to Remote Run.
UploadThe controller’s program comes back into the project. Changes made offline since the last download are lost; the controller keeps running.
CancelYou stay offline.

While online the two copies stay together. Communications → Require a download to go online is on by default; turned off, going online takes the project as it is, the way Logix Connect worked before. One habit from real machines: upload (or save the tag values) before a download if the controller holds values you need.

My Progress

Help → My Progress is a report on you rather than on the project: how far through the program you are, the levels done and how many under par, your best scores added up, the guided lessons finished and the fault drills run; the plant floor again; and a table of every level with its difficulty, status, best score, time against par, OEE and when you last played it. Without an account it is kept in this browser.

When the page can reach the bridge (the PC app, or a tablet on the bridge over Wi-Fi) it can keep accounts: after the splash you pick your name from the tiles and type your password, and each account keeps its own work in its own folder on the PC. A forgotten password is replaced by signing in with your PIN. The first account set up is the administrator. It keeps users out of each other’s work; it is not real security.
